TestCase_Name: Level Interrupt Active High - gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_39
TestCase_Description: Verify GPIO level-sensitive interrupt generation with active-high level selection. For each GPIO pin (8 through 39) configure the pin in input mode with level_sel=1 and nedge_intr_en=1 enable the corresponding group interrupt bit trigger the interrupt via SRAM stimulus and verify that the ISR fires through GIC IRQ 87.
Pre_Conditions: System reset completed. GIC initialized with IRQ 87 enabled. LSS sysreg intr_en1 gpio0_intr bit enabled.
Test_Steps: 1. Enable GIC IRQ 87 for GPIO0 interrupt routing. 2. Enable the GPIO0 interrupt bit in the LSS sysreg interrupt enable register (intr_en1). 3. For each GPIO pin (8 through 39) write to the per-pin GPIO register to set input mode with level_sel=1 and nedge_intr_en=1. 4. Enable the corresponding bit in the group interrupt enable register (gp0_intr1_intr_en1). 5. Write the trigger value to the SRAM stimulus address to generate a high-level signal. 6. Wait for the ISR to fire and set the interrupt pending flag to 0. 7. Repeat steps 3-6 for all 32 GPIO pins. 8. Verify that no errors were accumulated during the loop.
Expected_Result: For each GPIO pin the ISR fires successfully upon high-level stimulus. The interrupt pending flag is cleared by the ISR for all 32 pins.
Pass_Criteria: ISR triggers for each of the 32 GPIO pins. int_pend transitions from 1 to 0 for every iteration. test_err remains 0.
Notes: The test iterates over all 32 GPIO pins (8-39). Each pin is configured with 0x00180000 (bits 18 and 19 set = nedge_intr_en + level_sel). GIC IRQ 87 is used for GPIO0 instance. SRAM address 0xA0243ffc is used as the external stimulus trigger.

TestCase_Name: Level Interrupt Active Low - gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_39
TestCase_Description: Verify GPIO level-sensitive interrupt generation with active-low level selection. For each GPIO pin (8 through 39) configure the pin in input mode with level_sel=0 enable the corresponding group interrupt bit trigger the interrupt via SRAM stimulus with inverted pin mask and verify that the ISR fires through GIC IRQ 87.
Pre_Conditions: System reset completed. GIC initialized with IRQ 87 enabled. LSS sysreg intr_en1 gpio0_intr bit enabled. Active-high level interrupt test (TC_GPIO_013) completed.
Test_Steps: 1. For each GPIO pin (8 through 39) write to the per-pin GPIO register to set input mode with level_sel=0 (active-low configuration value 0x00100000). 2. Enable the corresponding bit in the group interrupt enable register (gp0_intr1_intr_en1). 3. Write the inverted pin mask to the SRAM stimulus address to generate a low-level signal on the target pin. 4. Wait for the ISR to fire and clear the interrupt pending flag. 5. Repeat steps 1-4 for all 32 GPIO pins. 6. Verify that no errors were accumulated during the loop.
Expected_Result: For each GPIO pin the ISR fires successfully upon low-level stimulus with inverted mask. The interrupt pending flag is cleared by the ISR for all 32 pins.
Pass_Criteria: ISR triggers for each of the 32 GPIO pins with active-low configuration. int_pend transitions from 1 to 0 for every iteration. test_err remains 0.
Notes: Active-low test uses 0x00100000 (only bit 20 = io_ctrl input mode level_sel bit 19 = 0). SRAM trigger uses ~(wr_val) to invert the pin mask generating a low-level signal on the specific pin. This is the second loop in test_case().

TestCase_Name: ISR Raw Interrupt Status Check and Interrupt Clear
TestCase_Description: Verify that within the ISR the per-pin GPIO register interrupt raw status bit is set when a level interrupt fires and that writing to the interrupt clear field successfully clears the raw status. After clearing verify the register reads the expected post-clear value.
Pre_Conditions: Level interrupt has been triggered on the GPIO pin. ISR (Default_IRQHandler) has been entered. The per-pin GPIO register has intr_raw_sts bit set.
Test_Steps: 1. Within the ISR read the per-pin GPIO register for the active pin. 2. Verify that the interrupt raw status bit (bit 1) is non-zero confirming the interrupt is pending. 3. Write the interrupt clear value (setting bit 16 and bit 20) to the per-pin GPIO register to clear the raw status. 4. Wait for the clear operation to take effect. 5. Read back the per-pin GPIO register. 6. Verify the read-back value equals the expected post-clear value (0x100001) confirming the interrupt was cleared and the pin returned to input mode with data_in reflecting the pin level.
Expected_Result: The interrupt raw status bit is set upon ISR entry. After writing the clear value the register reads 0x100001 (io_ctrl=1 in input mode data_in=1).
Pass_Criteria: Read of per-pin GPIO register shows intr_raw_sts (bit 1) != 0 before clear. After clear register reads exactly 0x100001. test_err is not incremented.
Notes: The ISR writes 0x00110000 to clear (bit 16 = intr_clr = 1 bit 20 = io_ctrl = 1 input mode). Expected post-clear read is 0x100001 (bit 20 = io_ctrl=1 bit 0 = data_in=1). If clear fails test_err is incremented.

TestCase_Name: Group Interrupt Enable and Status Verification
TestCase_Description: Verify that the group interrupt status register correctly reflects the interrupt status for the active GPIO pin when the corresponding group interrupt enable bit is set and that disabling the group interrupt enable clears the masked status to zero.
Pre_Conditions: Level interrupt has been triggered on the GPIO pin. ISR has been entered. Per-pin interrupt raw status confirmed set.
Test_Steps: 1. Within the ISR after confirming per-pin interrupt raw status read the group interrupt status register (gp0_intr1_intr_sts1). 2. Verify that the bit corresponding to the active GPIO pin is set in the group interrupt status. 3. After clearing the per-pin interrupt write 0x00000000 to the group interrupt enable register (gp0_intr1_intr_en1) to disable all group interrupts. 4. Read the group interrupt status register again. 5. Verify that the group interrupt status reads 0x0 (all bits cleared).
Expected_Result: Group interrupt status bit for the active pin is set when the interrupt is active. After disabling group interrupt enable the status register reads 0x0.
Pass_Criteria: Group interrupt status register has the active pin bit set (rdata_grp & (1<<i)) != 0. After disabling enable status reads 0x0. test_err is not incremented.
Notes: The ISR checks group status after confirming per-pin raw status. Group enable is disabled by writing 0x00000000 to gp0_intr1_intr_en1. If group status is not set when expected or not cleared when disabled test_err is incremented.

TestCase_Name: LSS Sysreg Raw Status Clear and Verification
TestCase_Description: Verify that the LSS sysreg raw status/clear register correctly reflects the GPIO0 interrupt and that writing the GPIO0 interrupt bit to the raw status/clear register successfully clears the sysreg-level interrupt status.
Pre_Conditions: GPIO interrupt has been triggered and confirmed at per-pin and group levels. ISR has been entered. Per-pin and group interrupts have been cleared.
Test_Steps: 1. Within the ISR after clearing per-pin and group interrupts write the GPIO0 interrupt bit value to the LSS sysreg raw status/clear register (raw_stcr1) to clear the sysreg-level interrupt. 2. Read back the raw status/clear register. 3. Verify that the GPIO0 interrupt bit is cleared (reads 0) in the raw status/clear register. 4. If the bit is not cleared record an error.
Expected_Result: After writing the GPIO0 interrupt bit to raw_stcr1 reading back the register shows the GPIO0 interrupt bit cleared to 0.
Pass_Criteria: Read-back of raw_stcr1 shows GPIO0 interrupt bit (bit 1) is 0 after the clear write. test_err is not incremented.
Notes: The RAWSTCR1 register type means: read returns raw interrupt status write 1 clears the corresponding bit.

TestCase_Name: GIC IRQ 87 Routing and ISR Execution
TestCase_Description: Verify that the GPIO0 interrupt is correctly routed through GIC IRQ 87 that the ISR (Default_IRQHandler) executes upon interrupt trigger and that GIC IRQ 87 is properly cleared at the end of the ISR to allow subsequent interrupts.
Field_Type: RW; RW; RW; RO; INTREN1; RAWSTCR1
Test_Steps: 1. Enable GIC IRQ 87 for GPIO0 interrupt routing. 2. Enable the GPIO0 interrupt bit in the LSS sysreg interrupt enable register. 3. Configure a GPIO pin for level-sensitive interrupt and enable the group interrupt. 4. Trigger the interrupt via SRAM stimulus. 5. Verify that the ISR (Default_IRQHandler) executes by confirming the interrupt pending flag is cleared. 6. Within the ISR verify the complete interrupt chain: per-pin raw status group status sysreg status. 7. Clear all interrupt levels in the ISR: per-pin clear group disable sysreg clear. 8. Clear GIC IRQ 87 at the end of the ISR. 9. Verify that subsequent interrupts can be triggered and handled (loop repeats for all 32 pins).
Expected_Result: GIC IRQ 87 correctly routes GPIO0 interrupts to the ISR. The ISR executes for each of the 32 GPIO pins in both active-high and active-low configurations. GIC clear allows subsequent interrupts.
Pass_Criteria: ISR fires for all 64 iterations (32 active-high + 32 active-low). All interrupt levels are verified and cleared. test_err remains 0. finish(test_err) reports PASS.
Notes: End-to-end test covering the full interrupt path: GPIO pin stimulus -> per-pin level_sel config -> group interrupt enable -> LSS sysreg enable -> GIC IRQ 87 -> ISR -> clear chain -> GIC clear.

TestCase_Name: SRAM Trigger Mechanism for GPIO Interrupt Stimulus
TestCase_Description: Verify that writing to the SRAM stimulus address generates the appropriate signal level on GPIO pins to trigger level-sensitive interrupts.
Pre_Conditions: GPIO pin configured for level-sensitive interrupt. Interrupt chain fully enabled (per-pin group sysreg GIC).
Test_Steps: 1. In the test_case function after configuring the GPIO pin and enabling the interrupt chain write 0xFFFFFFFF to the SRAM stimulus address to generate a high-level signal for active-high testing. 2. Verify that the interrupt fires (ISR is entered). 3. Within the ISR write 0xFFFFFFFF to the SRAM stimulus address to reset the stimulus state. 4. For active-low testing write the bitwise NOT of the pin mask to the SRAM stimulus address to generate a low-level signal on the target pin. 5. Verify that the interrupt fires for the active-low configuration.
Expected_Result: Writing to the SRAM stimulus address successfully generates the appropriate signal level on GPIO pins triggering level-sensitive interrupts in both active-high and active-low configurations.
Pass_Criteria: Interrupts are triggered for both active-high (0xFFFFFFFF) and active-low (~(1<<i)) SRAM writes. ISR fires and int_pend is cleared for each trigger.
Notes: SRAM address 0xA0243ffc is used as an external stimulus mechanism. This address is not mapped to any register in the specification documents.
